title: The Little Red Hen
strapline: From seed to loaf — who will help make the bread?
intent: The whole journey from wheat to bread is a story of process and sequence — planting, harvesting, grinding, baking.
The repeated 'Not I' from the lazy animals gives children a refrain to join in, and a hook for talk about helping and fairness.
Making real bread ties the tale to genuine cooking, change through heat and the satisfaction of a shared loaf.
The story raises early ideas of effort, contribution and reward in a way children feel keenly.
The farmyard becomes a small world for planting, working and baking together.
implementation: Set out the little red hen and the lazy animals, wheat to plant, and a mill and oven for the bread-making journey.
Tell the story with a chorus of 'Not I!', then let children play out the work — and choose whether their animals help.
Bake real bread alongside the story — measuring, kneading, waiting and sharing the warm loaf at the end.
Sequence the process together: 'What has to happen first? What comes after the wheat is cut?'
Open the fairness talk gently: 'The hen did all the work — should the animals get some bread? What do you think?'
Follow the children — some will bake and share, others will retell the story with the refrain again and again.
key_questions: What has to happen to turn wheat into bread — what comes first?
Who helped the hen, and who said 'Not I'?
Do you think the lazy animals should get any bread?
How does the dough change when it bakes?
How could the animals make it up to the hen?

impact.text: Children sequence the wheat-to-bread process and retell it with the refrain.
Children bake real bread and notice the dough changing as it cooks.
Children talk about helping, fairness and effort.
Children play out the farmyard work with roles and shared ideas.
Children share the loaf and take pride in what they made together.

enhancements: A real bread-making session — kneading, proving and baking, then sharing the warm loaf.
A wheat-to-bread sequencing set: seed, plant, harvest, grind, dough, loaf to put in order.
A grinding station — a pestle and mortar or a hand mill with grains to turn into flour.
Farmyard small-world figures for retelling with the 'Not I' chorus.
A helping-hands chart for the room, celebrating the children who pitch in.

playing_exploring: Children plant, grind, knead and bake, exploring every stage with their hands.
They play the farmyard, choosing whether their animals help the hen.
active_learning: Children see the long bread-making process through from grain to shared loaf.
They persist with kneading and waiting for the reward at the end.
creating_thinking: Children reason about the order of the process and what has to come first.
They form views about fairness and how the animals could put things right.
